chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding an insane woman who committed adultery and became pregnant: 'She is like the Sa'iba (unconditionally freed slave), she does not control her own affairs, and there is no stoning upon her, nor whipping, nor exile.'

And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a woman who testified against herself that a man forced himself upon her: 'She is like the Sa'iba, she does not control her own affairs; had he wished, he could have killed her. Therefore, there is no whipping upon her, nor exile, nor stoning.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him).
key_terms.السَّائِبَة: A slave woman freed unconditionally by her master, often used as a legal analogy for someone without a master to enforce punishment.
key_terms.جَلْد: Whipping/flogging, a punishment for unmarried adulterers.
key_terms.رَجْم: Stoning, a specific punishment for married adulterers.
key_terms.نَفْي: Exile, often accompanying the whipping punishment.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an insane woman who commits adultery according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic status of an insane woman committing adultery, equating her to the 'Sa'iba'—a slave manumitted unconditionally who is free from her master's authority—to justify her exemption from hadd punishments (stoning, whipping, and exile) due to impaired legal capacity. It further clarifies that even if she confesses to being coerced, her insanity renders her exempt from these specific corporal penalties, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'ajz' (inability) as a primary condition for waiving hadd. This ruling underscores the principle that punishment requires both the act and the conscious capacity to be held accountable, a key distinction in Usuli fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, fromMuhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said regarding an insane woman who committed adultery, so she became pregnant’. Heasws said: ‘She is similar to Al-Sa’aiba (unconditionally freed slave), having no control over her affairs, and there is neither stoning upon her, nor whipping, nor exiling’.

And heasws said regarding a woman who accepted upon herself that a man forced himself upon her. Heasws said: ‘She is similar to Al-Sa’aiba (unconditionally freed slave), not having control over her affairs. Had he so desired to, he could have killed her. Therefore, there is neither whipping upon her, nor exiling, nor stoning’.
